# Methodology {.unnumbered}

## Source materials

Materials in this edition were generated from the [compressed zip
file](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook.zip) available on the [CD
distribution page](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/cd.htm) of the
e-Handbook. The content of this file was compared against the e-Handbook's
online materials; discrepancies were few, and where they mattered they are
called out in the text of this edition.

- URL: <http://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/>
- Digital Object Identifier (DOI): <https://doi.org/10.18434/M32189>
- Zip file: <http://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook.zip>

## Code conventions

Code is intended to be pragmatic, readable, and — most importantly —
reproducible. New code favors functions from the
[tidyverse](https://www.tidyverse.org/) over base R or the original
Dataplot/S-PLUS scripts, which are retained alongside the original handbook
content for reference.

## Diagram conventions

Where possible, diagrams were recreated as SVG files (or as R/ggplot2
figures rendered directly from the chapter's own code), so that they can be
edited independently of any particular software program. Where it was not
practical to reproduce an original figure faithfully this way, the original
GIF image from the e-Handbook was retained instead.

## Review methodology

Every worked numerical example in this edition was checked against the
value reported in the original e-Handbook, generally by reproducing the
calculation in R (and, where one exists, cross-checking against the
e-Handbook's own companion Dataplot or R script). Genuine discrepancies
between the original text and the recomputed value are flagged in place
with a callout note, rather than silently corrected — the goal is to
preserve the original NIST content as the reference, while being transparent
about anywhere this edition's numbers diverge from it.

A full line-by-line comparison of the original archived materials against
this edition was not feasible — the original e-Handbook runs to more than
1,300 individual pages. Instead, each section was built and spot-checked for
accuracy as it was migrated, and whenever a deviation from the archived
material was detected, the surrounding section received a careful,
dedicated inspection. Undoubtedly, additional corrections will be needed as
this edition is used and reviewed more broadly — see `CONTRIBUTING.md` in
the repository for how to report them.

## Statement on the use of generative AI technologies

This edition was produced in close collaboration with
[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code), Anthropic's agentic coding
tool, working under the direction and review of the editor throughout.

For each chapter, the editor directed which section of the original
e-Handbook to migrate next; Claude Code then read the corresponding source
page(s) under `handbook/`, drafted the Quarto (`.qmd`) markdown and R code
reproducing the worked examples, executed that R code to verify every
reported numerical result against the original text, and rendered the
chapter to confirm the page built correctly before moving on. Genuine
discrepancies between NIST's published values and the recomputed ones were
flagged with callout notes rather than silently altered; the editor's own
transcription or formatting corrections were applied directly. Decisions
about structure, tone, visual conventions, and how to handle ambiguous or
inconsistent source material were made by the editor in the course of this
collaboration, and captured as standing conventions for the rest of the
project as they arose.

The editor reviewed each section as it was produced, spot-checked
calculations and rendering, and made the final call on anything flagged as
a discrepancy, an ambiguous judgment call, or a structural decision. As with
any large-scale migration of this kind, responsibility for the accuracy of
the final published content rests with the editor, not with the tool used
to help produce it.
